editorial:
Imagine walking into a high-stakes fashion casting where everything feels like a game. You have Henri, a casting director who loves to pull strings, and Yvan, a moody photographer who thinks he has seen it all. The vibe is tense and a bit strange, focusing on how these men treat the people they are hiring. Then comes Julie, a young woman who doesn't fit the usual mold. She is a mix of innocent and tough, and she quickly catches their attention. You will feel like you are spying on a private, uncomfortable conversation where nobody is being honest about what they actually want.

What really works here is how the movie shows the characters losing their grip on the truth. The acting feels real, and the way the camera lingers on the faces makes you feel the pressure Julie is under. While it moves a bit slow at times, the payoff is worth it for anyone who likes deep character studies. It is a great pick for a quiet night in.
endingExplained: By the end, Julie completely breaks down, showing her deepest fears and needs for attention. The power dynamic shifts as she stops playing the game and reveals her true self. The movie wraps up by showing that everyone was just using each other to feel important. It ends on a sad note, proving that the search for fame and recognition often costs you your own identity and peace of mind.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves movies about psychology and the dark side of the fashion world.
